variety: Bribri of Talamanca, Costa Rica. Same convention as src/content/drafts/bzd.json: headwords follow Krohn's pandialectal dictionary, preferring forms attested in Jara & García Segura (Coroma speech) and Margery (Amubri/Salitre data); dialect variants noted per card. Not checked for Panamanian Bribri.
orthography: Bribri practical orthography (Wilson, revised by Constenla; as used by Krohn, UCR and DIPALICORI): nasal vowels marked with a combining macron below (U+0331, the 'underline'), extra vowels ë ö; tone on the stressed syllable: acute = high/rising, grave = falling, circumflex = rising (Amubri); right single quote ’ = glottal stop; tk/tch variation as in the base draft. Strings stored NFC. Forms copied verbatim from Krohn's published XML data; Jara's newer tilde-nasal spelling is NOT used.

perro.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'perro', BRI→ES 'chìchi'; primary pages not verified)
perro.note: Single everyday form, no variants listed.
perro.reviewQuestion: Is chìchi the word children use for a dog?

pez.source: margery1996; flores2009; jaragarcia2013; chevrier2017 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'pez'; primary pages not verified)
pez.note: Variants ni̱mò̱, na̱mà̱, na̱mò̱ (dialectal a/o alternation in nasal syllables, as in kà̱li̱/kò̱li̱ 'rain').
pez.reviewQuestion: Which form is used in your community: ni̱mà̱, ni̱mò̱, na̱mà̱ or na̱mò̱?

venado.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; jaragarcia2003; flores2009 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'venado'; primary pages not verified)
venado.note: White-tailed deer specifically: të̀su̱li̱ (Sánchez s.f., Flores 2009). Old name dakë́k (Margery). Mild sensitivity: appears in the clan name Su̱lì̱tsuwak (Jara & García 2003); the plain animal noun is ordinary vocabulary.
venado.reviewQuestion: Is su̱lì̱ the everyday word for a deer, or would children say të̀su̱li̱?

mono.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; flores2009 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'mono'; primary pages not verified)
mono.note: No everyday generic 'monkey' word: the only generic is the hunters' term stsa’kichawak (Flores 2009). Species words: ö̀k capuchin, wìm howler monkey, sàl spider monkey (sàl also = 'spider', so avoided). ö̀k chosen; art should show a white-faced capuchin. Homonym ö̀k 'tiger heron' (Sánchez s.f.).
mono.reviewQuestion: For a generic monkey picture, which word would children use: ö̀k (cariblanco), wìm (congo) or sàl (colorado)?

murcielago.source: margery1996; flores2009; krohn2016 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'murciélago'; primary pages not verified)
murcielago.note: Variants dukúr, dkúr. Species compounds built on it (e.g. bàkadakur vampire bat).
murcielago.reviewQuestion: Which form is used: dakúr, dukúr or dkúr?

hormiga.source: margery1996; jaragarcia2013 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'hormiga'; primary pages not verified)
hormiga.note: Variants jtsàwak, tsáwak, kàlwak (Jara 2004). Many species names (kapalë’ leaf-cutter, alë̀r bullet ant). No anthill word found, so no collision with 'hormiguero'.
hormiga.reviewQuestion: Is stsàwak (or jtsàwak / tsáwak) the general word for ant in your community?

abeja.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'abeja', BRI→ES 'bùl'; primary page not verified)
abeja.note: Single source, glossed for the honey bee; variant bùlwak. A native small yellow stingless bee is kóswak (Jara & García 2003). Homonym bùl 'sorbón', a dance performed at chichadas (Margery) — check it is not felt as a ceremonial word.
abeja.reviewQuestion: Is bùl the general word for a bee, or is kóswak (stingless bee) better? Is there any ceremonial sense in bùl?

arana.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; chevrier2017 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'araña'; primary pages not verified)
arana.note: Variant ókwak. Alternative generic sàl / sàlwak (Sánchez s.f.) avoided because sàl also = spider monkey. Homonym ók 'tiger heron' (Margery, Rimolo).
arana.reviewQuestion: For a spider picture, do children say ók or sàl?

caracol.source: krohn2025 (searched ES lemma 'caracol' and Bribri definitions for caracol, babosa, molusco, Gastropoda)
caracol.note: Only marine conchs are attested: dúk 'caracol, cambute' (Strombus sp.) and pulë̀ (small conch). The card is a LAND snail and the deck forbids the conch trumpet, so these name a different thing. ipë’ / kachö̀tak = slug (no shell). Not substituting.
caracol.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a land snail with a shell? Would dúk or pulë̀ be used for it?

cangrejo.source: margery1996; flores2009; morales_com_pers (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'cangrejo'; primary pages not verified)
cangrejo.reviewQuestion: Which form is used: yawi’, yuwi’ or ywi’?

armadillo.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; jaragarcia2003; flores2009; sanchez_sf (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'armadillo'; primary pages not verified)
armadillo.note: Variants tsuì, tsuwì, tswì; synonym tö́töbe. Naked-tailed armadillo is bulùr.
armadillo.reviewQuestion: Which variant is used: tsawì, tsuwì or tswì?

lagartija.source: flores2009; jaragarcia2003 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'lagartija', BRI→ES 'kirë̀'; primary pages not verified)
lagartija.reviewQuestion: Is kirë̀ (or karrë̀ / krë̀) the general word for a small lizard?

perico.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'loro', BRI→ES 'tú̱li̱'; primary page not verified)
perico.note: Generic parrot word; ES index also lists yuri’ (Bozzoli 1977a). Small parakeets: ë̀l / kayö́ (Brotogeris, Margery) — kayö́ is also ritual speech for a song improviser, so avoided. Green macaw is apà.
perico.reviewQuestion: For a green parrot picture, do children say tú̱li̱, ë̀l, or another word?

raton.source: flores2009; jaragarcia2013 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'ratón'; primary pages not verified)
raton.note: Variant skuë̀. House mouse specifically: ùskuë (Flores 2009).
raton.reviewQuestion: Is sakuë̀ right, or would children say ùskuë for a house mouse?

gallina.source: jara2018; jaragarcia2013; margery1996; krohn2016; rimolo2007 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'gallina'; primary pages not verified)
gallina.note: Variants dakrò, dkrò, karò, korò, krò, tkrò. Covers hen and rooster; 'hen' specifically dakarò aláki (Margery). Introduced bird with a well-established Bribri name. Myth being Abèbulu 'king of the chicken' is unrelated; avoid.
gallina.reviewQuestion: Which form is used locally (dakarò, krò, tkrò…)?

arbol.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'árbol'; primary pages not verified)
arbol.reviewQuestion: Is kàl right for a picture of one tree?

hoja.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'hoja', BRI→ES 'kö̀'; primary page not verified)
hoja.note: Also 'hair', 'feather' (Constenla et al. 1998) and 'centipede'. Jara & García 2003 also list kö̀ as mythological 'little fire worms' — homonym. Inalienable form kö́yök. Single source for 'leaf'.
hoja.reviewQuestion: Is kö̀ how children name a single leaf?

flor.source: margery1996; constenla2015 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'flor', BRI→ES 'dakuà'; primary pages not verified)
flor.note: Synonyms mà̱ma̱ (also 'toy', 'ornament', affectionate 'mum'), mà̱ma̱dukà, mà̱ma̱wö. Same word noted in the base draft under 'girasol'.
flor.reviewQuestion: Do children say dakuà or mà̱ma̱ for a flower?

cacahuate.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'maní' or 'cacahuate'; Bribri definitions searched for maní/cacahuate)
cacahuate.note: No Bribri entry for peanut. No attested loan.
cacahuate.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri word for peanut (maní), or a Spanish loan in use?

raiz.source: jara2018; margery1996; jaragarcia2013 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'raíz', BRI→ES 'wì'; primary pages not verified)
raiz.note: Other words for root: cha̱lé̱, kichà, wìchle̱. kichà avoided (also = 'rope'). Tree root: kàlkichà.
raiz.reviewQuestion: Is wì the usual word for a root, or cha̱lé̱?

calabaza.source: chevrier2017; margery1996; jaragarcia2013 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'ayote', BRI→ES 'apì'; primary pages not verified)
calabaza.note: Variant pì. Krohn also lists kakö’ 'calabaza' (Margery), whose other sense is 'container for liquids' — likely the bottle gourd, so apì chosen for the edible squash.
calabaza.reviewQuestion: For an edible squash (ayote), is apì right? What is kakö’?

yuca.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; sanchez_sf (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'yuca'; primary pages not verified)
yuca.note: Variant li’. Homograph ali’ is also a verb form of alö́k 'cook'.

camote.source: margery1996; sanchez_sf (Krohn 2025 data, BRI→ES 'alabà'; primary pages not verified)
camote.reviewQuestion: Is alabà right for sweet potato?

guayaba.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, BRI→ES 'shu̱lé̱'; no ES lemma 'guayaba'; primary page not verified)
guayaba.note: Glossed as the tree 'guayabo'; fruit sense assumed, not stated. Not to be confused with shulú (guayabillo, Psidium sartorianum). Single source.
guayaba.reviewQuestion: Is shu̱lé̱ also used for the guava fruit?

algodon.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'algodón'; primary page not verified)
algodon.note: Variant suíyök. Cotton as material: sawi’ / sui’ (Margery). The card shows an open boll on a branch, so the plant word is chosen.
algodon.reviewQuestion: For a cotton boll on the plant, is sawíyök or sawi’ better?

huevo.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'huevo'; primary page not verified)
huevo.note: Single source for 'egg'; dùla also = 'little bird' (Margery) and 'delicacy' (Jara 2012b; Jara & García 2008). Hen's egg specifically: tkròla.
huevo.reviewQuestion: Is dùla the everyday word for an egg, or tkròla?

hongo.source: krohn2025 (ES lemma 'hongo' only lists bracket fungus; Bribri definitions searched for hongo/seta)
hongo.note: No generic word for mushroom. Attested only: ski’ / ski’kuö / kàlkukö / shkikukar 'oreja de palo' (bracket fungus on trunks, Polyporus sp.; Margery, Sánchez s.f.). The card is a plain cap mushroom, so these name a different thing. Sacred double: no Bribri ritual sense found, but unchecked.
hongo.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a cap mushroom? Could ski’ be used if the card showed a bracket fungus on a log?

platano.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'banano'; primary pages not verified)
platano.note: Variants chu̱mù̱, chmù̱. The English card is 'The Banana', so the banana word is chosen; cooking plantain is kalö́m (syn. kalö̀wö, tsalá).
platano.reviewQuestion: Should the card be cha̱mù̱ (banana) or kalö́m (plantain)?

pasto.source: margery1996; constenla2015 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'zacate', BRI→ES 'tàtsi'; primary pages not verified)
pasto.note: Variant tàtsikö. Constenla 2015 also uses it for a specific grass (Paspalum conjugatum).
pasto.reviewQuestion: Is tàtsi the word for grass/pasture?

papaya.source: sanchez_sf (Krohn 2025 data, BRI→ES 'skó̱kichö'; primary page not verified)
papaya.note: Generic papaya (and wild papaya, Carica peltata): kichö’ (Margery 1996). skó̱kichö is the cultivated species.
papaya.reviewQuestion: Do children say skó̱kichö or kichö’ for the papaya fruit?

fuego.source: margery1996; jaragarcia2003; krohn2016 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'fuego', BRI→ES 'bö̀wö'; primary pages not verified)
fuego.note: Also bö’ (Constenla et al. 1998), which also means 'firewood' (reserve card 'leña'); bö̀wö kept for fire to avoid the collision. bö̀wö also = 'light' (Jara & García 2003) and 'lamp' (Krohn 2016).
fuego.reviewQuestion: For a campfire picture, do children say bö̀wö or bö’?

humo.source: margery1996; constenla1998 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'humo'; primary pages not verified)
humo.reviewQuestion: Which form is used: shaka̱lá̱, shka̱lá̱ or shklá̱?

neblina.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'neblina'; primary page not verified)
neblina.note: WORD COLLISION: mò̱ is already the name of the existing card 'nube' (cloud). Under deck rule 8 only one can stay in Bribri; this card should be unavailable in Bribri unless a reviewer gives a distinct fog word.
neblina.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for fog that differs from mò̱ (cloud)?

granizo.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'granizo'; Bribri definitions searched)
granizo.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri word for hail?

nieve.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'nieve'; Bribri definitions searched)
nieve.note: No Bribri entry for snow (not part of the Talamanca lowland environment).
nieve.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri word for snow, or a Spanish loan in use?

hielo.source: krohn2016; morales_com_pers (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'hielo'; primary pages not verified)
hielo.note: A modern descriptive form recorded in Krohn's lexical-acculturation study, not a traditional word. Not analysed or translated here.
hielo.reviewQuestion: Do people actually say di’wö sí for ice? How is it pronounced?

amanecer.source: krohn2025 (ES lemma 'amanecer' lists verbs only; Bribri definitions searched for amanecer/alba/aurora/madrugada)
amanecer.note: Only verbs are attested: ka̱ñí̱nu̱k (Pacchiarotti 2014) and shkè̱nu̱k (Margery) 'to dawn'. No noun 'dawn'; using a verb form for a picture card is a reviewer decision, not proposed here.
amanecer.reviewQuestion: Can ka̱ñí̱nu̱k or shkè̱nu̱k be used as the name of a 'dawn' picture, or is there a noun?

noche.source: jara2018; jaragarcia2013; margery1996; chevrier2017 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'noche', BRI→ES 'na̱ñé̱we'; primary pages not verified)
noche.note: Mostly attested as an adverb 'de noche' (variant na̱ñè̱e); Margery also 'last night'. Only Chevrier 2017 gives a noun sense 'darkness'. No plain noun 'night' found.
noche.reviewQuestion: Is na̱ñé̱we natural as the name of a 'night' picture?

cielo.source: margery1996; morales_com_pers (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'cielo', BRI→ES 'ká̱költtö'; primary pages not verified)
cielo.note: Variants ká̱kólttö, ká̱ttö, kó̱ttö; ká̱ttö also = 'ravine, slope' (Jara & García 2015; Jara 2018). SENSITIVITY: the sky has a cosmological sense in Bribri tradition (layered world); confirm the everyday word is fine for a game.
cielo.reviewQuestion: Is ká̱költtö the everyday word for the sky, and is it acceptable in a game?

sombra.gloss: shadow (of people and animals); also reflection, image, picture
sombra.source: margery1996; jaragarcia2003 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'sombra', BRI→ES 'diö́köl'; primary pages not verified)
sombra.note: Glossed for shadows of people and animals, while the card shows a tree's shade. SENSITIVITY: Jara & García 2003 also give 'alma de los ojos' (a spiritual sense). àlim 'mala sombra' is an illness term — do not use.
sombra.reviewQuestion: Is diö́köl used for the shade of a tree, and is it acceptable given its spiritual sense?

rocio.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'rocío'; Bribri definitions searched for rocío/sereno)
rocio.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri word for dew?

remolino.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'remolino' or 'torbellino'; Bribri definitions searched)
remolino.note: No Bribri entry for whirlwind. Not deriving from su̱wa̱’ 'wind' (which also has a sacred-history sense).
remolino.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri word for a whirlwind?

agua.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'agua'; primary pages not verified)
agua.note: di’ also means 'river'; the river card uses dìkibi to avoid a collision. Ritual-speech dipàkala (García com. pers.) must NOT be used.
agua.reviewQuestion: Is di’ right for a drop of water?

ceniza.source: margery1996; chevrier2017; jaragarcia2003 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'ceniza'; primary pages not verified)
ceniza.reviewQuestion: Which form is used: ma̱lù̱chaka, mlù̱shka or mu̱lù̱?

trueno.source: margery1996; chevrier2017 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'trueno'; primary pages not verified)
trueno.note: Variant lá. Ritual-speech tkë́rme̱ must NOT be used. SENSITIVITY: thunder is tied to mythological beings (see the base draft's 'rayo' note); the plain noun should be fine but confirm.
trueno.reviewQuestion: Is alá the everyday word for thunder, and acceptable in a game?

rio.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'río', BRI→ES 'dìkibi'; primary page not verified)
rio.note: Synonyms di’ (also 'water', the 'agua' card) and di’ula (Jara 1993; Morales com. pers.). dìkibi chosen to avoid colliding with 'agua'. Tributary: ulà.
rio.reviewQuestion: Do children say dìkibi or di’ula for a river?

lago.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'laguna', BRI→ES 'batsö̀ri'; primary page not verified)
lago.note: Variant btsö̀ri. Other 'laguna' words avoided: dapö̀ (also 'pool in a river' and 'palmito') and dö́ (also 'mud', the 'lodo' card).
lago.reviewQuestion: Is batsö̀ri used for a lake or lagoon?

piedra.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; chevrier2017 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'piedra'; primary pages not verified)
piedra.note: Plain everyday noun; homonym 'kidney'. SENSITIVITY: the sacred healing stones (si̱a̱’, duwàl, dikúswa and ritual names) must NOT be used. Card must show an ordinary grey stone.
piedra.reviewQuestion: Is ák fine for an ordinary stone in a game?

arena.source: margery1996; garcia_com_pers (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'arena'; primary pages not verified)
arena.note: Variants stsa̱’, tsa̱’, tsa̱’ña̱, tsá̱ña̱. Beach sand: dayë̀tsa̱ña̱.
arena.reviewQuestion: Which form is used: stsa̱’ña̱, tsa̱’ña̱ or stsa̱’?

playa.source: margery1996; flores2009 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'playa'; primary pages not verified)
playa.note: Variant dyë̀jkö. Other 'playa' words: tsà̱itö 'playa, arenal' and ákitö 'river beach' (Margery). dayë̀jkö chosen as the sea beach.
playa.reviewQuestion: For a sea beach, do children say dayë̀jkö or tsà̱itö?

cascada.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'cascada'; primary page not verified)
cascada.note: Synonym yö̀l, which also means 'stream or jet of water' (Chevrier 2017). Single source for 'waterfall'.
cascada.reviewQuestion: Do children say yö̀lukö or yö̀l for a waterfall?

charco.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'charco'; Bribri definitions searched for charco/poza)
charco.note: No word for a rain puddle. dapö̀ / di’dape mean a pool in a river (poza), a different thing.
charco.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a small rain puddle?

lodo.source: jara2018; margery1996; jaragarcia2013; chevrier2017 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'barro'; primary pages not verified)
lodo.note: Variants dö́chaka, dö́chika, dö́chka. Also glossed 'pantano' (Rimolo 2007) — collides with the 'pantano' card.

barranca.source: constenla1998 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'barranco', BRI→ES 'ká̱böl'; primary page not verified)
barranca.note: Synonyms àsir (also 'landslide'), balë́ (depression in the ground), dìböl (ravine, river channel), ká̱ttö (also 'sky' — avoided). ká̱böl has only the ravine sense.
barranca.reviewQuestion: Which word would children use for a ravine: ká̱böl, àsir or dìböl?

llano.source: margery1996; garcia_com_pers (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'llanura'; primary pages not verified)
llano.note: ajkuè 'small plain' (Constenla 2010, place names). sö̀k 'savanna' (Margery) is a different landscape.
llano.reviewQuestion: Is ká̱jkue̱ the word for open flat land?

pantano.source: rimolo2007; margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'pantano'; primary pages not verified)
pantano.note: WORD COLLISION: same word as the 'lodo' card. Under deck rule 8 only one can stay in Bribri. Related adjective abòbò 'swampy' (Margery) is not a noun.
pantano.reviewQuestion: Is there a separate word for a swamp, different from dö́ (mud)?

ola.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'ola'; Bribri definitions searched for ola/olas/oleaje/marejada)
ola.note: No Bribri entry for a sea wave.
ola.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri word for a wave of the sea?

concha.source: garcia_com_pers (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'concha'; primary page not verified)
concha.note: Single source (personal communication). Variants dayë̀pulë̀, dayë̀plë, diyë̀pulë, diyë̀plë. Built on pulë̀ 'small conch'. Avoid tsiríkö (shells or leaves used by healers, Jara & García 2003).
concha.reviewQuestion: Is dayë̀pulë the everyday word for a seashell on the beach?

valle.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'valle'; Bribri definitions searched for valle/hondonada/cañada)
valle.note: No generic word for valley; only place names and clan names (Su̱lì̱tsuwak).
valle.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri word for a valley?

tierra.source: jara2018; jaragarcia2013; margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'tierra'; primary pages not verified)
tierra.note: SENSITIVITY: the ritual-speech form irìria (Constenla 2006) is linked to the mythological girl from whom the earth was made — must NOT be used. íyök is the everyday noun; card shows soil, not the Earth.
tierra.reviewQuestion: Is íyök fine for a picture of soil?

hacha.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'hacha'; primary page not verified)
hacha.reviewQuestion: Is o’ the word for an axe?

red.source: krohn2025 (ES lemma 'red' only lists net bags; Bribri definitions searched for red/malla/atarraya/pesca)
red.note: No word for a fishing net. sakú / saku’ / kala’ are net BAGS (used for the 'morral' card). Traditional fishing used traps (a̱lò̱) and river drying (di’ síwè̱), not nets.
red.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a fishing net (or cast net)?

cuerda.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'cuerda (trenzada)', BRI→ES 'búsköl'; primary page not verified)
cuerda.note: Chosen because the general rope words ja̱mù̱, kichà, stsa’ collide: ja̱mù̱ is the existing 'hilo' card and kichà also = 'root'. Card art is a thick coiled rope, which fits 'braided rope'. Alternative dakuë̀ (rope or braided hair).
cuerda.reviewQuestion: For a thick rope, do children say búsköl, stsa’ or ja̱mù̱?

jicara.source: margery1996; jaragarcia2013; chevrier2017 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'guacal'; primary pages not verified)
jicara.note: Variants tko̱’; synonym skò̱tke̱ (Chevrier). Small one: datsù. Tree: mè̱. SENSITIVITY: calabash bowls are used to serve ceremonial cacao; the card must show an everyday bowl.
jicara.reviewQuestion: Is tka̱’ the everyday word for a calabash bowl, and is a game card with it acceptable?

metate.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'metate'; primary page not verified)
metate.note: Single source. Grinding verb wö́k; wooden roller for grinding wàwè (Jara 2018).
metate.reviewQuestion: Is ákajkue still used for a grinding stone?

comal.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'comal'; Bribri definitions searched for comal/tiesto/budare/plancha)
comal.note: No noun for a griddle; only verbs 'toast, roast' (ijkuö̀k, kujkuö̀k).
comal.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a clay or metal griddle?

escoba.source: chevrier2016 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'escoba'; primary page not verified)
escoba.note: Single source; variant ùshklö. túskicha is a palm (escoba palm), not the broom.
escoba.reviewQuestion: Is ùshkalö the word for a broom?

aguja.source: margery1996; chevrier2016 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'aguja'; primary pages not verified)
aguja.reviewQuestion: Is dika’ used for a sewing needle?

huso.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'huso' or 'malacate'; Bribri definitions searched for huso/hilar/tejer/torcer)
huso.note: No Bribri entry for spindle or spinning.
huso.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a spindle used to spin cotton?

banco.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; jara2013 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'asiento', BRI→ES 'kula’'; primary pages not verified)
banco.note: Everyday seat. SENSITIVITY: kulékala is a special seat used by a first-time mother and her husband (Constenla 2015; García com. pers.) — must NOT be used. The ES 'banco' lemma is the financial institution (i̱nú̱köl wé), not this card.
banco.reviewQuestion: Is kula’ the everyday word for a wooden stool, with no ceremonial sense?

sombrero.source: constenla1998 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'sombrero'; primary page not verified)
sombrero.note: Variant tsà̱kuö. Descriptive synonym wö́kir ajkuö̀ / wö́kirkuö recorded in Krohn 2016 (lexical acculturation).
sombrero.reviewQuestion: Is tsà̱jkuö used for a woven hat?

morral.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'bolso', BRI→ES 'saku’'; primary pages not verified)
morral.note: Variant sku’. Larger net bag sakú (Margery); cabuya backpack bíssku (Margery); small-object net bag kala’.
morral.reviewQuestion: For a carry bag, do children say saku’ or bíssku?

hamaca.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; chevrier2017 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'hamaca'; primary pages not verified)
hamaca.note: Variants kipö̀, kpö̀. Homonym kapö̀ 'tree fern' (Margery).
hamaca.reviewQuestion: Which form is used: kapö̀, kipö̀ or kpö̀?

coa.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'coa' or 'espeque'; Bribri definitions searched for sembrar/espeque/chuzo/macana)
coa.note: No noun for a digging/planting stick; only verbs 'to plant' (kuátkök, tkö́k).
coa.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for the planting stick (espeque)?

petate.source: jara1987 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'estera', BRI→ES 'ùkö'; primary page not verified)
petate.note: Single source. Homonym ùkö 'cola de gallo' shrub (Aphelandra scabra), same source.
petate.reviewQuestion: Is ùkö the word for a woven sleeping mat?

camino.source: jaragarcia2013; margery1996; jaragarcia2003 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'camino'; primary pages not verified)
camino.reviewQuestion: Which form is used: ña̱là̱ or ño̱lò̱?

pozo.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'pozo'; Bribri definitions searched)
pozo.note: No word for a dug well. 'Pozo' appears only in definitions of mythological beings living in water holes (Alákilirma̱, Ö̀rösili; Jara & García 2003) — sensitive context. tù̱m 'spring' is the existing 'manantial' card.
pozo.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a dug water well? Are water holes culturally sensitive?

nido.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'nido', BRI→ES 'dù ù'; primary page not verified)
nido.note: Single source; written as two words. Contains ù 'house' (the 'casa' card) — check players can tell them apart.
nido.reviewQuestion: Is dù ù how children say bird's nest?

colmena.source: jaragarcia2003 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'colmena'; primary page not verified)
colmena.note: Single source, from the mythology dictionary; check the word has no ritual sense. Related to bùl 'bee'.
colmena.reviewQuestion: Is bùbul the everyday word for a beehive, without a mythological sense?

hormiguero.source: krohn2025 (ES lemma 'hormiguero' only lists anteater and antbirds; Bribri definitions searched)
hormiguero.note: No word for an anthill. urrì = anteater, kaë̀yöwö = antbird — different things.
hormiguero.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for an anthill or ant nest?

telarana.source: garcia_com_pers (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'telaraña'; primary page not verified)
telarana.note: Single source (personal communication). Uses sàl 'spider' (which also = spider monkey) + ù 'house'; the 'arana' card uses ók instead — reviewer should check consistency.
telarana.reviewQuestion: Is sàl ù how people say spider web? Should the spider card then be sàl instead of ók?

patio.source: margery1996; constenla1998 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'patio'; primary pages not verified)
patio.note: Alternative ùjkö / ùkkö (Jara 2012b) avoided because it is also the 'puerta' card. Base draft already noted ù apà under 'plaza'.
patio.reviewQuestion: Is ù apà the usual word for the yard around a house?

huerto.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'huerto' or 'huerta'; Bribri definitions searched for huerto/jardín/solar)
huerto.note: No word for a kitchen garden distinct from të̀ 'cultivated plot', which is the existing 'milpa' card.
huerto.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a small garden next to the house, different from të̀?

cerca.gloss: fence; also floor, wall, raised bed
cerca.source: margery1996; jaragarcia2013; jara1987 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'cerca'; primary pages not verified)
cerca.note: Variants ako̱’, ko̱’. 'Fence' sense is from Margery; Jara & García 2013 and Jara 1987 give 'floor', 'wall', 'tapesco/bed'. Polysemous.
cerca.reviewQuestion: Is aka̱’ understood as a fence when shown on its own?

puerta.source: jara2013; chevrier2017; margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'puerta'; primary pages not verified)
puerta.note: Variant ùkkö. Jara 2012b also glosses ùjkö as 'patio'; the patio card uses ù apà to avoid the collision.
puerta.reviewQuestion: Is ùjkö the word for a door?

techo.source: jara1987; morales_com_pers (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'techo'; primary pages not verified)
techo.note: Outer roof: ù tsì̱ (Margery); inner ceiling: ù ttö (Jara 1987). Contains ù 'house'.
techo.reviewQuestion: For a thatched roof, do children say ù kibì or ù tsì̱?

escalera.source: jaragarcia2013 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'escalera'; also listed with synonyms from margery1996, sanchez_sf, morales_com_pers; primary pages not verified)
escalera.note: Synonyms kàlwökichi (Margery; Morales com. pers.) and pi̱ská (Sánchez s.f. -b, DIPALICORI).
escalera.reviewQuestion: For a notched-log ladder, do children say tí̱ska, pi̱ská or kàlwökichi?

troje.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'troje' or 'granero'; Bribri definitions searched for granero/troje/despensa/tapanco)
troje.note: No Bribri entry for a granary or storehouse.
troje.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a place where maize is stored?

cocina.source: margery1996; chevrier2017 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'cocina'; primary pages not verified)
cocina.note: Variant bö́kkö. Synonyms bö̀we (Chevrier 2016) and ù̱lök 'kitchen (part of a house)' (Jara 1987).
cocina.reviewQuestion: For a kitchen hut, do children say bö́jkö, bö̀we or ù̱lök?

corral.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'corral'; Bribri definitions searched for corral/cercado/potrero)
corral.note: No word for a livestock corral. kö̀chiwe 'pigsty' (Margery) names a different enclosure.
corral.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for an animal pen, or would kö̀chiwe be used?

gusano.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'gusano'; primary page not verified)
gusano.note: Synonym í̱ (also 'earthquake', avoided). Earthworm: í̱ña̱ (Margery, Flores) or tsi̱mí̱ño̱ (Sánchez s.f.).
gusano.reviewQuestion: For a worm picture, do children say ö́ña̱, í̱ña̱ or tsi̱mí̱ño̱?

zorro.source: krohn2025 (ES lemma 'zorro' lists opossums and a skunk only; Bribri definitions searched for coyote/Urocyon)
zorro.note: In Costa Rican Spanish 'zorro' is the opossum: bikili’ / bakali’ (Didelphidae) — a different animal from a fox. bikili’ also means the interpreter for the high priest (uséköl), a sacred role. No fox word found. Do not substitute.
zorro.reviewQuestion: Is there a Bribri word for a fox (gray fox)? Or should the card show an opossum (bikili’) instead?

pato.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'pato'; primary page not verified)
pato.note: Variant duák. Single source; species-specific but the common duck of the region.
pato.reviewQuestion: Is dawák used for ducks in general?

luciernaga.source: margery1996; jaragarcia2003 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'luciérnaga'; primary pages not verified)
luciernaga.note: Variant ktù; synonym tkö̀wö / tkö’wö (Constenla 2010; Margery 2017). Listed in the mythology dictionary: check for a mythological sense.
luciernaga.reviewQuestion: Do children say katù or tkö̀wö for a firefly? Any mythological sense?

cantaro.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'cántaro' or 'tinaja'; Bribri definitions searched)
cantaro.note: No word for a water jar distinct from ù̱ 'pot' (the existing 'olla' card). The clan name ù̱ni̱wak 'owners of the clay jar' (Jara & García 2003) is sacred/social, not usable.
cantaro.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a clay water jar different from ù̱?

pelota.source: constenlapereira1989 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'pelota', BRI→ES 'kàlwö'; primary page not verified)
pelota.note: Also 'fruit of a tree' (Margery). The ES index also lists bola (Jara 2013), a Spanish loan.
pelota.reviewQuestion: Do children say kàlwö or bola for a ball?

collar.source: margery1996 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'collar', BRI→ES 'bë́wö'; primary page not verified)
collar.note: Synonyms kuli’io (Margery), balë̀wö (Chevrier). balë̀ / balë̀wö also mean 'menstruation' (Margery) — avoided. tà̱u̱ is the high priest's necklace — sacred, must NOT be used.
collar.reviewQuestion: Is bë́wö the everyday word for a bead necklace?

cuchara.source: krohn2016 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'cuchara'; primary page not verified)
cuchara.note: Recorded in the lexical-acculturation study as an extension of ulàtsika 'finger' (Jara 1993); the same word is given for 'fork'. A card showing a hand-like sense would break the no-body-parts rule; art must show only a spoon.
cuchara.reviewQuestion: Is ulàtsika really used for a spoon, or is a Spanish loan more common?

remo.source: krohn2025 (no ES lemma 'remo'; Bribri definitions searched for remo/remar/canalete)
remo.note: No Bribri entry for paddle or oar.
remo.reviewQuestion: Is there a word for a canoe paddle?

sal.source: margery1996; sanchez_sf (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'sal'; primary pages not verified)
sal.note: WORD COLLISION: dayë̀ is already the existing 'mar' card. Under deck rule 8 only one can stay in Bribri. Variants diyë̀, dyë̀.
sal.reviewQuestion: Is there a separate word for salt, different from dayë̀ (sea)?

semilla.source: jara2018 (Krohn 2025 data, BRI→ES 'kuö̀wö'; primary page not verified)
semilla.note: SENSITIVITY: the commoner synonym ditsö̀ / ditsö̀wö also means 'clan', 'race' and 'the first Bribris' (Jara & García 2003), the seeds brought by Sibö̀ in Bribri creation narratives — avoided. wö̀ 'fruit, seed' also means 'face' — avoided.
semilla.reviewQuestion: Is kuö̀wö natural for a seed, or do children say ditsö̀wö? Is ditsö̀ appropriate for a game?

lena.source: constenla1998 (Krohn 2025 data, ES→BRI 'leña', BRI→ES 'bö’'; primary page not verified)
lena.note: Single source, which also glosses bö’ as 'fire'. Close to bö̀wö (the 'fuego' card) — possible confusion.
lena.reviewQuestion: Is bö’ understood as firewood (not fire)? Is there another word?
